data.title: A small clinic with one aim
data.intro: MoveWell is a physiotherapy clinic for people who want to move comfortably and keep doing what they enjoy.

children.text: How we work
Every visit starts with a conversation. We want to know what you do in a normal week and what you want to get back to, then we plan around that.
Sessions are one to one and last 45 minutes. You see the same physiotherapist each time, so you do not have to retell your story.
What we do not do
We do not promise outcomes or sell long packages up front. We book a visit, see how you respond and plan the next step together. If physiotherapy is not what you need, we say so.
Where to find us
We are on Harbour Lane in Seaton Bay, a short walk from the bus stop. The treatment rooms are on the ground floor and have step-free access.

data.title: Your first visit
data.intro: What to wear, what to bring and what to expect when you come in for the first time.

children.text: Before you come
Wear clothes you can move in, such as shorts or loose trousers and a t-shirt. If your problem is in your shoulder, bring a vest top or sports top.
Bring a list of medicines you take, and any scan reports, discharge notes or letters from your doctor or surgeon.
At the clinic
Please arrive five minutes early to fill in a short form. Your physiotherapist will start by asking about your history, then check how you move before any treatment.
Cancelling or changing
Tell us at least 24 hours ahead if you need to change a time. You can phone, or reply to your confirmation email.

data.title: Injury Rehabilitation
data.summary: A plan to get you moving again after a sprain, strain or overuse injury.
data.best_for: Adults with a recent or lingering injury
data.visit:
We talk through what happened and what you want to get back to
A hands-on check of movement, strength and where it hurts
Treatment and a few exercises to start with
A written plan and when to book the next visit
data.how_to_book: Send a request from the contact page and the front desk will reply with times. Leave medical details out of the form, you can talk them through at the visit.
data.tile_text:
Get back to the activities
you enjoy.

children.text: Injuries rarely need a long list of exercises. They need the right few, done in the right order, and a plan for building back up.
What we look at
We start with the story: how it happened, what makes it worse and what you do in a normal week. Then we check how the area moves and how strong it is next to the other side.
What happens next

You leave with a short exercise plan and a clear idea of what to avoid for now. Follow-up visits are shorter and focus on changing the plan as you improve. Some injuries need a doctor's opinion first, and we will tell you if that is the case.

data.title: Mobility & Flexibility
data.summary: Stretching, joint mobility and simple routines for stiffness that has built up over time.
data.best_for: Adults who feel tight or stiff day to day
data.visit:
We ask where you feel stiff and when it is worst
A movement screen of hips, back, shoulders and ankles
Hands-on work and guided stretches
A routine of five to eight minutes you can do at home
data.how_to_book: Send a request from the contact page and the front desk will reply with times. Leave medical details out of the form, you can talk them through at the visit.

children.text: Stiffness often comes from doing the same things all day: sitting, driving, carrying the same bag on the same shoulder. This visit looks at how your joints move and where they could move more.
In the room
Expect to move a lot. We try positions, note what feels tight and what is simply weak, and pick stretches that suit your body rather than a generic list.
At home
The routine we give you is short on purpose. Five minutes you will actually do is worth more than twenty you skip.

data.title: Posture & Movement
data.summary: A look at how you sit, stand and move, with small changes for desk and daily life.
data.best_for: Desk workers, drivers and anyone with a sore neck or back
data.visit:
We talk through your day: desk, commute, hobbies, sleep
We watch you sit, stand, walk and lift
Hands-on treatment where it helps
A few habit changes and exercises to practise
data.how_to_book: Send a request from the contact page and the front desk will reply with times. Leave medical details out of the form, you can talk them through at the visit.
data.tile_text:
Build better habits
for a healthier you.

children.text: There is no single correct posture. What matters is that you change position often and that your body is ready for the positions you hold longest.
What we change
Usually small things: screen height, how you lift, how long you stay in one spot. We write them down so you can try them at work and at home.
Follow-up
A second visit two to three weeks later lets us check what has stuck and adjust the plan.

data.title: Sports Physio
data.summary: Assessment and treatment for training injuries, with a plan to build back safely.
data.visit:
We ask about your sport, training load and the injury
Tests for strength, balance and the movement that hurts
Treatment and a modified training plan
A step-by-step plan for returning to your sport
data.how_to_book: Send a request from the contact page and the front desk will reply with times. Leave medical details out of the form, you can talk them through at the visit.
data.tile_text:
Back to training,
step by step.

children.text: Training injuries usually come from a mix of load, recovery and technique. We look at all three instead of resting the sore spot and hoping.
Bring
Wear what you train in and bring your shoes if the issue is running. A training diary or watch history is useful if you have one.

data.title: Post-Surgery Rehab
data.summary: Guided rehabilitation after orthopaedic surgery, following your surgeon's instructions.
data.best_for: People recovering from joint or soft tissue surgery
data.visit:
We read any notes or protocol from your surgeon
We check range of movement, swelling and strength
Treatment and exercises suited to your stage
A schedule of visits that matches your protocol
data.how_to_book: Send a request from the contact page and the front desk will reply with times. Leave medical details out of the form, you can talk them through at the visit.

children.text: Rehabilitation after surgery follows your surgeon's protocol. Our job is to help you work through it safely and to tell the surgical team if something does not look right.
Before you book
Please bring any discharge notes or rehab protocol to the first visit. If you do not have them, ask your surgeon's office to send them.

data.title: Balance & Strength
data.summary: One-to-one sessions that build leg strength and steadiness for everyday tasks.
data.best_for: Older adults and anyone who feels unsteady on their feet
data.visit:
We talk about what feels difficult: stairs, getting up, walking outside
Simple tests of balance, leg strength and walking
Guided exercises with support nearby
A home plan with options for harder and easier days
data.how_to_book: Send a request from the contact page and the front desk will reply with times. Leave medical details out of the form, you can talk them through at the visit.

children.text: Staying strong enough to get out of a chair, climb stairs and carry shopping is something you can train at any age.
How we work
Exercises are chosen from what you want to do. We keep a chair or bar within reach at all times, and we progress slowly.
